newsitem.title: FRANCE: Publicis quotes scripture in Pope campaign.
newsitem.headline: Publicis quotes scripture in Pope campaign.

text.p: Publicis, the French advertising agency, is running an unusual campaign for the visit to France next week by Pope John Paul II, a Publicis executive said on Wednesday.
The campaign, which also promotes a six-day international festival being organised by the Catholic Church, called World Youth Days, borrows lines straight from the Bible.
French radio stations, press publications and billboard owners have donated space to run the ads.
"There isn't really an advertising message. It is an unusual campaign," said Arnaud Gufflet, head of advertising at Publicis.

Publicis picked three lines from the Gospels -- "Love thine enemy", "Arise and have no fear" and "Hope cannot disappoint" -- for three posters, carried as a white banner headline on a blue background with text underneath inviting young people to join in the event.
The lines from the Bible are being repeated in ads on the radio and in the cinema.
"The idea was to address society as a whole and not just young Catholics," Gufflet said.
The agency created an Internet site for the event at http://www.cef.fr/jmj97, which offers an audio message from the Pope.
The advertising campaign began with press adverts in February, the cinema spot ran in May and June, posters appeared across France in June, and the radio spot started last month, Gufflet said.
Publicis sent a compact disc of the radio spot to representatives of the World Youth Days throughout France and they sought space for the advert on local stations, he said.
France Telecom's teletext service, Minitel, carries information on it under the code name Gabriel.
World Youth Days open in Paris on August 19, and the Pope arrives on August 21.
